summary: [Digital Morocco 2030](2025-07-31 Morocco Digital Economy — US Country Commercial Guide (Digital Morocco 2030)) has been in force since September 2024 and picked up a [US$250m acceleration programme](2026-07-22 Morocco to Launch $250 Million World Bank-Backed Digital Transformation Program) in June 2026.
developments:
The strategy's stated targets include a place in the global top 50 for electronic government and 100,000 people trained by 2030, and the technology sector was 6.8 per cent of gross domestic product on a 2025 figure ([strategy](2025-07-31 Morocco Digital Economy — US Country Commercial Guide (Digital Morocco 2030))).

A US$250m programme was attached to it in June 2026 ([programme](2026-07-22 Morocco to Launch $250 Million World Bank-Backed Digital Transformation Program)). Two held sources give the 2030 jobs target as 150,000 and as 240,000, and the base holds no progress report against any of the targets ([programme](2026-07-22 Morocco to Launch $250 Million World Bank-Backed Digital Transformation Program)).

summary: The [5G licence specification](2025-07-22-anrt-rapport-instruction-licences-5g) carries the country's only published coverage commitments: a quarter of the population by end-2026 and 70 per cent by 2030.
developments:
The regulator's own instruction report sets a coverage floor of eight cities plus airports by November 2025, 25 per cent of the population by the end of 2026 and 70 per cent by the end of 2030, on a maximum of three twenty-year renewable licences ([instruction report](2025-07-22-anrt-rapport-instruction-licences-5g)).

It corrects a conflicting figure held elsewhere in the base. The bidders' own coverage commitments are not disclosed in the report, and no separate national broadband plan is held.

summary: A [Cloud First policy](2025-01-01 Morocco adopts Cloud First Policy under Digital Morocco 2030) makes cloud the mandatory default for public technology investment, and a [cloud roadmap to 2030](2025-11-01-ausim-livre-blanc-cloud-au-maroc) sits behind it without published targets.
developments:
The policy made cloud the mandatory default for public-administration technology investment, with a national cloud observatory scheduled for 2027 that is not established ([policy](2025-01-01 Morocco adopts Cloud First Policy under Digital Morocco 2030)).

The roadmap sets six objectives and twenty-one intervention domains, a national cloud marketplace through the development agency, sovereign cloud under the qualification decree, and a national reference architecture promised from 2026; its claimed economics are a fifth to a third off procurement cost and MAD 100bn by 2030, and its formal targets, budget and milestones are still absent ([roadmap](2025-11-01-ausim-livre-blanc-cloud-au-maroc)).

summary: The [AI Made in Morocco roadmap](2026-01-30-industries-ma-maroc-ia-2030-roadmap-programmes) names a digital commons platform, a twenty-interface library and once-only exchange, on a trade-press account rather than a published text.
developments:
A trade-press account of January 2026 sets out ten programmes under the roadmap, of which the data and interoperability strand names a digital commons platform, a library of twenty application interfaces and a once-only principle ([programmes](2026-01-30-industries-ma-maroc-ia-2030-roadmap-programmes)).

No ministry document setting out an interoperability framework or roadmap has been published, so the strand is on record only as reported and carries no timetable, custodian or list of participating administrations ([roadmap](2026-03-11-techafricanews-ai-made-in-morocco-industry-x0)).

summary: An [AI Made in Morocco roadmap](2026-01-12-mtnra-ai-made-in-morocco-jazari-root-launch) has been named by the ministry since January 2026, and no text of it has been published.
developments:
The roadmap was named at a national event on 12 January 2026, framed there as consolidating the country's 2030 artificial-intelligence programme, and repeated at subsequent signings ([launch](2026-01-12-mtnra-ai-made-in-morocco-jazari-root-launch), [seminar](2026-03-11-techafricanews-ai-made-in-morocco-industry-x0)).

A trade-press account describes ten programmes across trust, infrastructure, data, skills and a national Darija and Amazigh language model at alpha stage ([programmes](2026-01-30-industries-ma-maroc-ia-2030-roadmap-programmes)). No roadmap document is on file: every reference is a ministry statement.

summary: Sensitive data must be [hosted exclusively on national territory](2020-08-06-morocco-loi-05-20-cybersecurite), a [cloud qualification decree](2025-02-20-morocco-decret-2-24-921-prestataires-cloud) awaits its implementing order, and a [classification guide](2026-01-11 The Year of the Teeth Data Protection in Africa Roundup, 2025, Projections for 2026) sets the categories.
developments:
Law 05-20 article 11 mandates exclusive national hosting of sensitive data and article 49 sets a fine of MAD 200,000 to 400,000, doubled on repeat, while article 53 defers force to implementing texts and the definition of sensitive data sits in an unheld decree ([law](2020-08-06-morocco-loi-05-20-cybersecurite)).

Decree 2-24-921 was gazetted in February 2025 and is not in force: neither the qualification order nor the list of qualified providers is held, and level-2 qualification would require processing and storage exclusively on national territory and Moroccan majority ownership ([decree](2025-02-20-morocco-decret-2-24-921-prestataires-cloud)).

A national data classification guide categorises data by sensitivity and requires sensitive data to be stored domestically; its own text, issuing body and date are not held ([guide](2026-01-11 The Year of the Teeth Data Protection in Africa Roundup, 2025, Projections for 2026)).

summary: The open-data programme has [four published procedure volumes](2024-12-01-add-maroc-manuel-operationnel-standards-formats-donnees-ouvertes) and a four-strand action plan, with a steering committee of ten bodies established in December 2019.
developments:
The published procedure set runs to manuals for open-data officers and data managers from April 2021, a data-inventory methodology from February 2023 and a standards and formats manual from December 2024 ([inventory methodology](2023-02-01-add-maroc-guide-methodologique-inventaire-de-donnees), [standards manual](2024-12-01-add-maroc-manuel-operationnel-standards-formats-donnees-ouvertes)).

A steering committee of ten bodies was established in December 2019 and a readiness assessment carried out in 2020, after which a four-strand action plan covering legal, technical, organisational and usage work was adopted ([governance](2026-08-08-data-gov-ma-gouvernance-plan-actions-national-open-data)). The assessment report itself is not held.

summary: [Law 09-08](2026-08-04-protection-des-donnees-la-confiance-moteur-de-leconomie-numerique) has been in force since 2009, and the regulator states on the record that a recast is now in the legislative circuit.
developments:
The commission's president stated in August 2026 that a recast developed with the justice ministry has been sent to the government's general secretariat, describing it as clarification rather than replacement ([statement](2026-08-04-protection-des-donnees-la-confiance-moteur-de-leconomie-numerique), [account](2026-08-09-maroc-data-centers-leader-ia)).

No transmission date or text is held ([framework bill](2025-11-04-wearetech-morocco-landmark-law-ai-data-identity)). The statute's own text and gazette reference are not held either, nor any amending instrument, and a 2023 amendment survives only as an analyst's attributed statement ([guide](2025-07-31 Morocco Digital Economy — US Country Commercial Guide (Digital Morocco 2030))).

summary: [Law 05-20 on cybersecurity](2020-08-06-morocco-loi-05-20-cybersecurite) has been in force since July 2020, with its own article 53 deferring effect to implementing texts the base does not hold.
developments:
The law sets outsourcing conditions in article 12 and penalties in article 49, and defers its force to implementing texts in article 53 ([law](2020-08-06-morocco-loi-05-20-cybersecurite)).

The decree defining the sensitive data the law turns on is not held, so the statute is on the books and the base cannot establish which processing it reaches. No prosecution, enforcement action or compliance count under it is recorded.

summary: [Law 72-18](2021-01-07-maroc-loi-72-18-ciblage-appui-social-agence-nationale-registres) creates the population and social registries, the civil and social digital identifier and the register agency, deferring force to implementing texts.
developments:
The statute was promulgated by dahir in August 2020 and creates the national population register, the unified social register, the civil and social digital identifier and the national register agency ([law](2021-01-07-maroc-loi-72-18-ciblage-appui-social-agence-nationale-registres)).

Articles 19 and 22 carve out defence and security processing, and article 45 defers force to implementing texts. The base holds no implementing decree, so the identifier's legal operation cannot be established from the statute alone.

summary: A [Digital X.0 framework bill](2025-11-04-wearetech-morocco-landmark-law-ai-data-identity) sits with the government's general secretariat on three pillars, one of them interoperability on traceable consent.
developments:
The bill was under review by the general secretariat in November 2025, on pillars of data governance, sectoral digital identity, and interoperability resting on traceable consent ([bill](2025-11-04-wearetech-morocco-landmark-law-ai-data-identity), [account](2025-11-06 Morocco prepares 'Digital X.o' draft law (AI governance, sectoral digital IDs, interoperability))).

The ministry frames it as sitting under the 2009 data-protection law rather than replacing it. No text, article count or tabling date is on record, and nothing has been published about it since.

summary: The [electoral organic law](2026-07-30-morocco-criminalising-ai-disinformation-2026-elections) carries the only enacted artificial-intelligence offences, while a [private members bill](2025-01-09-hespress-morocco-ai-legislative-initiative) on regulating the technology has not moved.
developments:
Organic law 53.25 enumerates artificial-intelligence tools as a means of commission on four electoral offences and creates a new article punishing the fabrication of election disinformation with two to five years and a fine of MAD 50,000 to 100,000, upheld against a press-freedom challenge ([offences](2026-07-30-morocco-criminalising-ai-disinformation-2026-elections)). The constitutional court found nothing unconstitutional in December 2025 ([decision](2025-12-24-maroc-cour-constitutionnelle-decision-259-25-loi-organique-53-25), [tabling](2025-10-24-morocco-projet-loi-organique-53-25-chambre-des-representants)).

A seventeen-article private member's bill setting fines of MAD 50,000 to 500,000 has been before the chamber's bureau since January 2025 with no committee report ([bill](2025-01-09-hespress-morocco-ai-legislative-initiative), [roundup](2026-01-11 The Year of the Teeth Data Protection in Africa Roundup, 2025, Projections for 2026)).

summary: [Law 31-13](2018-05-03-maroc-loi-31-13-droit-acces-information-bo-6670) has been in force since 2018 and the commission it created publishes no annual reports, though its own article 22 requires them.
developments:
The law was promulgated by dahir in February 2018 and created the access-to-information commission, with article 30 deferring entry into force by a year and proactive-publication duties by a further year ([law](2018-05-03-maroc-loi-31-13-droit-acces-information-bo-6670)).

The commission publishes no annual reports despite the duty in article 22, so eight years on the base holds the statute, the institution and no measure of requests made, granted or refused under it.

summary: The commission runs a [public national register](2023-01-11-cndp-communique-publication-registre-national-rn-pdp) of declared processing under the 2009 law and signed a [cooperation memorandum with Portugal](2026-06-23 Bimonthly Update on Privacy in Africa (January & February 2026)) in February 2026.
developments:
The data-protection authority set out in a communiqué of 28 August 2026 the rules binding political parties, candidates and artificial-intelligence-generated content during the legislative campaign ([communiqué](2026-08-31-fr-legislatives-2026-la-cndp-encadre-lusage-des-donnees)), having earlier set out the requirements for processing personal data in the elections ([guidance](2026-08-29-morocco-cndp-election-data-protection-guidance)).

The national register was first published in January 2023, covering installations from the commission's own creation to the end of 2022, with a definitive-format version in February 2023 and a separate complaints and controls register public from March 2023, operating under articles 45 to 50 of the law ([register](2023-01-11-cndp-communique-publication-registre-national-rn-pdp)).

A cooperation memorandum with the Portuguese authority was signed on 8 February 2026, covering exchange of information and technical expertise on artificial intelligence, synthetic media and digital violence; the text is not held ([memorandum](2026-06-23 Bimonthly Update on Privacy in Africa (January & February 2026))).

progress: Regressed, live facial recognition entered field service with no authorisation, legal basis or retention rule cited in either account held
summary: [Smart patrol vehicles](2026-07-21-assabah-dgsn-aman-madar-smart-patrol-facial-recognition) carrying live facial recognition entered service in Rabat in July 2026, five years into a [case-by-case authorisation regime](2020-12-30-cndp-deliberation-d-195-eus-2020-usage-reconnaissance-faciale) whose public-highway question is still open.
developments:
The commission replaced a lapsed moratorium with a case-by-case prior-authorisation regime at the end of 2020, conditioning future authorisation on routing through a national trusted-third-party identity system and flagging controllers building their own biometric databases, sometimes hosted abroad ([regime](2020-12-30-cndp-deliberation-d-195-eus-2020-usage-reconnaissance-faciale)).

It decided hearings on video surveillance in March 2025 and had published no deliberation by August 2026, treating facial recognition on the public highway as an open question ([hearings](2025-03-21-cndp-communique-videosurveillance-protection-donnees-personnelles)).

Patrol vehicles with live facial recognition, automated number-plate reading and in-vehicle access to the central database entered field service in Rabat in the week of 20 July 2026, with two further cities announced; neither held account cites a data-protection authorisation, a legal basis, a retention rule or an oversight mechanism ([patrols](2026-07-21-assabah-dgsn-aman-madar-smart-patrol-facial-recognition), [account](2026-07-23-maroc-patrouilles-police-ia)).

summary: Morocco was [elected to the African Telecommunications Union council](2026-07-25-morocco-elected-african-telecommunications-union-council) for 2027-2031 and signed digital instruments with [Gabon](2026-04-13-techafricanews-morocco-gabon-digital-skills) and [Ghana](2026-05-11-techafricanews-morocco-ghana-statement-of-intent).
developments:
The seat was won at the union's twenty-sixth plenipotentiary conference in July 2026, on a delegation combining the digital ministry, the regulator and the development agency; the country offered three of its own programmes to other African states at the same conference ([election](2026-07-25-morocco-elected-african-telecommunications-union-council)).

A protocol with Gabon on digital skills was signed at a Marrakech exhibition in April 2026, with capacity-building commitments directed at Gabon and no value, term or timetable stated ([protocol](2026-04-13-techafricanews-morocco-gabon-digital-skills)).

A statement of intent with Ghana covering digitalisation, open government, artificial intelligence, data governance and exchanges of experts was signed in Rabat in May 2026, again with no value or term ([statement](2026-05-11-techafricanews-morocco-ghana-statement-of-intent)).

[A memorandum with the UN Economic and Social Commission for Western Asia, signed in Rabat in September 2026, establishes a framework for regional cooperation on modernising public administration and advancing digital governance reform](2026-09-03-techafricanews-escwa-morocco-digital-governance-mou). No programme, value or deliverable is stated for it.

summary: Host-country agreements were approved for a [continental development agency office](2026-06-02-assabah-rabat-cybersecurity-leadership-program) and a [regional cyber-incident centre](2026-06-02-assabah-rabat-cybersecurity-leadership-program), and the country joined a [cross-border rails pilot](2026-05-26-nigeria-kenya-morocco-afcfta-adapt).
developments:
Both host-country agreements were approved by the council of ministers on 9 April 2026; the development agency office is not on record as established, and the cyber-incident coordination centre has no site, budget, staffing or opening date ([office](2026-06-02-assabah-rabat-cybersecurity-leadership-program), [centre](2026-06-02-assabah-rabat-cybersecurity-leadership-program)).

Morocco was selected in May 2026 as one of the first three countries to implement shared cross-border rails for identity, payments and trusted data exchange, on a two-stage assessment of political commitment, regulatory alignment, technical capacity, private-sector engagement and the maturity of national digital systems; no Moroccan implementation plan, budget or timetable is published ([pilot](2026-05-26-nigeria-kenya-morocco-afcfta-adapt)).

summary: [Continental data-exchange guidelines](2025-07-14 Smart Africa co-creates Africa's first Cross-Border Data Exchange Guidelines (Rabat, ADD-chaired CAITA)) drafted under Moroccan chairmanship remain unpublished, a [ledger-based pilot](2026-05-28 Building the same road twice) names the country, and [Convention 108](2012-10-18-coe-tpd-2012-09rev-avis-adhesion-maroc-convention-108) has been ratified since 2019.
developments:
Eleven member states convened in Rabat in July 2025 to draft the continent's first cross-border data exchange guidelines under Moroccan chairmanship of the agency council, and no guidelines were on record a year later ([drafting](2025-07-14 Smart Africa co-creates Africa's first Cross-Border Data Exchange Guidelines (Rabat, ADD-chaired CAITA))).

Morocco is one of three pilot states for a cross-border data exchange on a distributed-ledger reference architecture owned by the continental trade secretariat, with no Moroccan implementing body, start date or budget named ([pilot](2026-05-28 Building the same road twice)).

Convention 108 was ratified during 2019; the Council of Europe's 2012 opinion named two defects in the domestic law, its exclusion of public-safety and law-enforcement processing and a definition of sensitive data omitting sexual life and criminal convictions, and the base holds no record that either was closed ([opinion](2012-10-18-coe-tpd-2012-09rev-avis-adhesion-maroc-convention-108)).

progress: Mixed, published median speeds fell through the first year of 5G while the binding quality annex of the licences stays confidential
summary: [Median mobile speeds fell](2026-08-03-ookla-5g-north-africa-one-year-on) through the first six months of 5G, and the quality-of-service annex of the [licences](2025-11-06-morocco-decret-2-25-876-5g-licence-itissalat-al-maghrib) is withheld as confidential though binding.
developments:
A measurement firm's series puts the 5G median down 38 per cent from 261.7 Mbps at launch to about 160 to 165 Mbps at month six, the 4G median down 28 per cent, and the combined median at 44.59 Mbps against 44.4 Mbps a week before launch ([measurements](2026-08-03-ookla-5g-north-africa-one-year-on)).

Three licences were awarded and gazetted individually, and the specification's five annexes on shareholding, frequencies, coverage engagements, quality of service and interference procedure are withheld as confidential though binding, with the Arabic text prevailing in court ([licences](2025-11-06-morocco-decret-2-25-876-5g-licence-itissalat-al-maghrib), [tender](2025-07-16-telecomreviewafrica-morocco-5g-license-tender)). The regulator stated it would assess operators after the first operational year.

summary: The national information-security directive is [structured on an international standard](2023-01-12-dgssi-circulaire-02-2023-directive-nationale-securite-si-v2), and the new [biometric passport](2026-07-15-biometricupdate-morocco-biometric-passport-legal-framework) carries a chip to the civil aviation standard.
developments:
Circular 02/2023 put version 2.0 of the national information systems security directive in force, structured on ISO 27002, covering state bodies and all infrastructures of vital importance, with entities given six months to schedule conformity ([directive](2023-01-12-dgssi-circulaire-02-2023-directive-nationale-securite-si-v2)).

The passport decree approved in July 2026 specifies an encrypted chip to the International Civil Aviation Organization standard and four languages including Amazigh ([decree](2026-07-15-biometricupdate-morocco-biometric-passport-legal-framework), [account](2026-07-10-en-hespress-morocco-new-biometric-passport-amazigh)). No conformity count, certification register or audit against either standard is held.

progress: No change, a first record of the debate with nothing earlier behind it
summary: A [public argument for statutory platform responsibilities](2026-08-16-hespress-ceuta-events-digital-sovereignty-challenges) was made in the press in August 2026 by an association specialist and a researcher, against blanket blocking.
developments:
A cybersecurity specialist from a digital-trust association and a social researcher argued that unrest had exposed gaps in the country's platform-regulation framework, warning against blanket platform blocking or breaking encryption and calling instead for statutory platform responsibilities, notice-and-response mechanisms and account-verification rules ([argument](2026-08-16-hespress-ceuta-events-digital-sovereignty-challenges)).

It is commentary rather than a state position, no such bill is held, and the base records no earlier instance of organised non-governmental input into digital policy against which to set it.

summary: The [ombudsman](2026-08-24-morocco-ombudsman-calls-public-debate-administration-reform) called publicly in August 2026 for administrative reform to be made one policy under a single lead, after [finding agencies still demanding paper](2026-08-16-morocco-administrative-digitization-ombudsman-report) the law says they may not.
developments:
The ombudsman's 2025 report found agencies still asking for paper copies of documents already held electronically and imposing undisclosed extra conditions, contrary to the simplification law; the finding reaches the record through a member's written question to the ministry, and no ministry answer is held ([report](2026-08-16-morocco-administrative-digitization-ombudsman-report)).

A vigilance memorandum of 24 August 2026 calls for simplification, digitisation and deconcentration to be coordinated as one workstream under a single, clearly located government lead, and proposes a national system for evaluating administrative performance on service quality, ease of access, delivery times, user satisfaction and how far administrations act on complaints ([memorandum](2026-08-24-morocco-ombudsman-calls-public-debate-administration-reform)). The measurement architecture it proposes does not exist.

progress: No change, no appropriation published since the 2024 line
summary: The ministry's own series stops at a [MAD 1,758.7m investment appropriation for 2024](2024-01-01-maroc-mtnra-budget-annuel-dotations-par-chapitre), with no 2025 or 2026 figure published.
developments:
The 2024 investment line stands at MAD 1,758.7m against MAD 85.8m for personnel and MAD 187.8m for materiel, and is the latest year in the ministry's published budget-by-chapter series ([series](2024-01-01-maroc-mtnra-budget-annuel-dotations-par-chapitre)).

The same series runs MAD 11.7m in 2021, MAD 246.7m in 2022 and MAD 1,249.2m in 2023 ([series](2024-01-01-maroc-mtnra-budget-annuel-dotations-par-chapitre)), so the investment line grew by two orders of magnitude in three years and then stopped being published.

summary: Three vendor frameworks are on file and none carries a sum: with [Orange on artificial intelligence](2026-06-05-techafricanews-morocco-orange-ai-partnership), on a [private 5G laboratory](2026-04-08-techafricanews-orange-maroc-ericsson-collaboration), and with [Vodafone Business](2025-04-25-itweb-vodafone-maroc-telecom-digital-services-deal).
developments:
The ministry signed with Orange in Casablanca on 4 June 2026 at a second artificial-intelligence summit, advancing the institutes programme with no sum attached ([memorandum](2026-06-05-techafricanews-morocco-orange-ai-partnership)).

A vendor agreed to supply a private 5G platform for an operator laboratory at an April 2026 exhibition, with a catalogue targeting smart logistics, utilities and energy ([agreement](2026-04-08-techafricanews-orange-maroc-ericsson-collaboration), [exhibition](2026-04-10-connectingafrica-gitex-africa-2026-morocco-deals)).

A memorandum with Vodafone Business signed in April 2025 for smart-city and energy-management solutions has had no delivery, expansion or sum reported since ([framework](2025-04-25-itweb-vodafone-maroc-telecom-digital-services-deal)).

summary: A [corporate venture fund](2026-08-02-techtrends-african-corporate-venture-capital-banks) of US$250m is reported operating, writing cheques of up to US$5m into regional start-ups.
developments:
The fund was reported operating in August 2026, with no establishment date on file ([report](2026-08-02-techtrends-african-corporate-venture-capital-banks)).

The figure is attributed by the reporting outlet to a third-party tracker and no Moroccan disclosure is on file, so the base holds a private commitment of that size on one indirect account and nothing on what it has deployed.

summary: A [US$250m digital transformation programme](2026-07-22 Morocco to Launch $250 Million World Bank-Backed Digital Transformation Program) was approved in June 2026, alongside a [US$70m identity and targeting project](2024-12-04 World Bank approves $70M for Morocco's social protection delivery (RNP and Unified Social Registry)) and an earlier [EUR 459.8m policy loan](2020-05-26 Morocco First Financial and Digital Inclusion Development Policy Financing (World Bank)).
developments:
The acceleration programme is US$250m over five years, approved and signed in June 2026 with effectiveness targeted before 23 September 2026 and conditions for entry into force outstanding ([programme](2026-06-01-world-bank-mar-2026-morocco-digital-transformation-acceleration), [account](2026-07-22 Morocco to Launch $250 Million World Bank-Backed Digital Transformation Program)).

A second identity and targeting project of US$70m was approved in December 2024 with no disbursement or delivery reported since ([project](2024-12-04 World Bank approves $70M for Morocco's social protection delivery (RNP and Unified Social Registry))).

A first financial and digital inclusion policy loan of EUR 459.8m was issued in May 2020 and no second operation in the series is on file ([loan](2020-05-26 Morocco First Financial and Digital Inclusion Development Policy Financing (World Bank))); the base holds the programme document and no completion or results report ([loan](2020-05-26 Morocco First Financial and Digital Inclusion Development Policy Financing (World Bank))).

progress: Mixed, subscriber numbers rose while measured 5G speed fell
summary: The regulator's own observatory puts the [mobile park at 57.06m and penetration at 154.93 per cent](2026-06-19-anrt-observatoires-telecoms-maroc-t1-2026), with the park down slightly year on year and [5G in service](2025-11-08-hespress-morocco-5g-launch-new-digital-era) since November 2025.
developments:
Independent measurement put median 5G speed down 38% in six months, from an opening figure near 267 Mb/s ([measurement](2026-08-27-bladi-morocco-5g-speed-decline-ookla)) — a fall in service quality as subscriber numbers rise.

The first regulator-published periodic observatory, for the first quarter of 2026, gives a mobile park of 57.06m, down 0.58 per cent year on year, penetration of 154.93 per cent, outgoing traffic down 18.79 per cent and messaging down 9.12 per cent, with sector revenue up 2.89 per cent ([observatory](2026-06-19-anrt-observatoires-telecoms-maroc-t1-2026)).

Three operators launched 5G on the same day in November 2025 on 3.5 GHz and 700 MHz ([launch](2025-11-08-hespress-morocco-5g-launch-new-digital-era), [account](2025-11-07-en-hespress-what-5g-could-mean-for-morocco)).

A dual-band deployment on rail and motorway corridors entered commercial service in 2026 with no additional sites built; the regulator put that operator at 19.4m mobile subscriptions and a 34.04 per cent share at the end of March 2026 ([deployment](2026-08-13-morocco-inwi-huawei-transport-route-coverage)).

summary: [5G reached 3.2m subscribers](2026-08-03-ookla-5g-north-africa-one-year-on) by March 2026, 8.4 per cent of mobile-internet users, from 2.63m at the end of 2025.
developments:
The regulator's figures, as reported by a measurement firm, give 3.2m 5G subscribers at March 2026 and 8.4 per cent of mobile-internet users, up from 2.63m and 38 per cent outdoor population coverage at the fourth quarter of 2025 ([figures](2026-08-03-ookla-5g-north-africa-one-year-on)).

Morocco is the only market in that comparison publishing a 5G subscriber count, which is itself the finding: the number exists here and nowhere else in the set.

summary: [Mobile interconnection tariffs](2026-07-22-maroc-telecom-rapport-financier-semestriel-2026) entered a transitional reduction in July 2026 and reach full symmetry in February 2027.
developments:
The transitional phase runs from 1 July 2026 to 31 January 2027, with full symmetry from 1 February 2027 ([phase](2026-07-22-maroc-telecom-rapport-financier-semestriel-2026)).

The record of it is the operator's own half-year filing; the regulator's decision text is not held, and no retail price, basket or affordability measure for the country is held at all.

summary: [Fibre to the home reached 1.5m lines](2026-06-19-anrt-observatoires-telecoms-maroc-t1-2026), about half of wireline internet, with [passive sharing](2026-07-22-maroc-telecom-rapport-financier-semestriel-2026) opening commercially and [joint ventures](2025-04-02-connectingafrica-maroc-telecom-inwi-fiber-5g) holding shared assets.
developments:
The regulator's first-quarter 2026 observatory gives fixed lines at 3.262m, up 5.05 per cent, and fibre to the home at 1.5m, about 52 per cent of wireline internet ([observatory](2026-06-19-anrt-observatoires-telecoms-maroc-t1-2026)).

Technical prerequisites for passive infrastructure sharing were completed in April 2026 with commercial opening scheduled for 27 April over a 40,000-line lot ([sharing](2026-07-22-maroc-telecom-rapport-financier-semestriel-2026)); the date is the operator's own filing and no source confirms the opening happened ([sharing](2026-07-22-maroc-telecom-rapport-financier-semestriel-2026)).

Two operators formed joint ventures on shared fibre and mobile-site assets in April 2025, with no further reporting on file; the regulator flagged uneven low-density coverage as a risk of the shared model ([joint ventures](2025-04-02-connectingafrica-maroc-telecom-inwi-fiber-5g)).

summary: The [Medusa subsea cable](2025-07-28-itweb-nokia-subsea-cable-europe-north-africa) selected its optical supplier in July 2025 and no Moroccan landing date has been published.
developments:
The supplier was selected in July 2025 and nothing further is on file; the system was announced in 2022 and landing agreements are held with licensed local operators ([supplier](2025-07-28-itweb-nokia-subsea-cable-europe-north-africa)).

No capacity, price or utilisation figure for international bandwidth is held for the country, so the base records one cable in progress and no measure of what the country already has.

progress: Mixed, an incumbent terminal licence renewed to 2035 while the low-orbit operator is still unlicensed
summary: [Starlink has no licence](2026-03-16-morocco-starlink-anrt-status-medias24) eighteen months after incorporating a local subsidiary, while a [satellite terminal licence](2026-07-22-maroc-telecom-rapport-financier-semestriel-2026) was renewed in February 2026 to 2035.
developments:
The subsidiary was incorporated in November 2024 with capital of MAD 1,000 and still had no authorisation in May 2026, with regulator negotiations reported continuing and the operator's own map listing the service date as unknown ([status](2026-03-16-morocco-starlink-anrt-status-medias24), [subsidiary](2026-04-16-morocco-starlink-subsidiary-maroc-hebdo), [observation](2026-05-20-morocco-starlink-observation-anrt-challenge)).

A licence requires a competitive call under the telecommunications law and security clearance, which is the procedural reason the base records rather than a refusal.

The incumbent's satellite terminal licence was renewed in February 2026 for a further ten years to 2035 ([renewal](2026-07-22-maroc-telecom-rapport-financier-semestriel-2026)).

progress: Mixed, a new certified facility in service against a national capacity figure six years old and no reliable estate count
summary: There is [no national facility count with an established counting rule](2023-09-01-conseil-concurrence-monographie-sectorielle-datacenters); the state's last capacity measurement is [98 MW for 2020](2023-08-31-cese-avis-71-2023-cloud-levier-urgence-transformation-digitale), and one [1.5 MW facility](2025-11-24-techafricanews-orange-maroc-sustainable-data-center) opened in 2025.
developments:
The widely repeated count of twenty-three, said to put the country ahead of South Africa, is a September 2023 tally of facilities certified by one institute, not a current census; other published counts use unstated rules and are not commensurable with it or with each other ([monograph](2023-09-01-conseil-concurrence-monographie-sectorielle-datacenters), [comparison](2025-06-09-en-hespress-morocco-overtakes-sa-top-data-center-hub)).

The economic and social council's national series ends at 98 MW installed in 2020, of which 14 MW was outsourced, and runs 52 MW in 2014, 79 MW in 2018 and 88 MW in 2019; no later national figure has been published ([series](2023-08-31-cese-avis-71-2023-cloud-levier-urgence-transformation-digitale)).

An operator inaugurated a data centre at Nouaceur in November 2025 at 1.5 MW initial capacity, certified, with more than 1,000 solar panels ([facility](2025-11-24-techafricanews-orange-maroc-sustainable-data-center)).

summary: A [sovereign compute programme](2026-04-08-mtnra-nexus-ai-factory-plateform-maroc) commits MAD 12bn over two phases, with a [Dakhla campus](2025-11-18-techreviewafrica-morocco-green-data-center-ai-institute-dakhla), a [Rabat sovereign centre](2026-07-27-morocco-mtnra-vertiv-mou-communique) and a [supplier memorandum](2026-07-27-morocco-mtnra-vertiv-mou-communique) behind it.
developments:
The ministry's April 2026 figures are MAD 12bn over two phases, MAD 5bn for 16 MW at Nouaceur and MAD 7bn for a further 20 MW in the north, giving 36 MW cumulative and 125 direct jobs by end-2027 ([platform](2026-04-08-mtnra-nexus-ai-factory-plateform-maroc)). A 2025 consortium release had put phase one at over 40 MW, so phase-one capacity has been reduced ([release](2025-06-18-nexus-core-lloyds-consortium-500mw-ai-factory)).

A green data-centre campus at Dakhla was agreed in November 2025, with one part for sovereign needs and one open to private investment, and feasibility studies launched in April 2026 ([campus](2025-11-18-techreviewafrica-morocco-green-data-center-ai-institute-dakhla)).

A sovereign data centre at Rabat, announced in October 2025 on a single trade-press account, is named in the ministry's July 2026 communique as a project a supplier cooperation will feed, still with no cost, site or date ([communique](2026-07-27-morocco-mtnra-vertiv-mou-communique), [memorandum](2026-07-30-vertiv-signs-mou-with-morocco-to-develop-sovereign-digital-infrastructure)).

progress: No change, the contracted power figure is unchanged and the ministry's own restatement omits it
summary: Up to [500 MW is contracted](2025-06-18-nexus-core-lloyds-consortium-500mw-ai-factory) for the compute programme, against [36 MW of cumulative capacity](2026-04-08-mtnra-nexus-ai-factory-plateform-maroc) planned by the end of 2027.
developments:
A strategic agreement for up to 500 MW was announced in June 2025 and the ministry's April 2026 communique restates no power-supply figure ([agreement](2025-06-18-nexus-core-lloyds-consortium-500mw-ai-factory), [communique](2026-04-08-mtnra-nexus-ai-factory-plateform-maroc)).

The 500 MW is contracted power supply and not installed compute, which is the distinction the press accounts collapse ([platform](2026-04-08-mtnra-nexus-ai-factory-plateform-maroc)). No water assessment for any site is held, and no national statement connects data-centre demand to generation capacity.

summary: The [Court of Cassation portal](2026-08-07-morocco-court-cassation-website-outage) went offline for more than a week in August 2026 with no official explanation, on a bar-association account.
developments:
The portal lawyers use to track rulings was reported down for over a week on 7 August 2026, as the courts increasingly rely on digital portals for that purpose ([outage](2026-08-07-morocco-court-cassation-website-outage)).

The outage and the criticism of the silence around it are a lawyer's account; no court or ministry statement is held, and the base holds no availability, incident or recovery measure for any other government system.

summary: A [national cybersecurity strategy to 2030](2024-01-01-dgssi-strategie-nationale-cybersecurite-2030) sets four pillars and sixty actions, above a [security directive](2023-01-12-dgssi-circulaire-02-2023-directive-nationale-securite-si-v2) in force since 2023 and a [response centre](2026-06-21-hespress-morocco-fortibleed-macert-cyber-alert) issuing advisories.
developments:
The strategy carries four pillars, eleven objectives, twenty-six initiatives and sixty actions, succeeding the country's first strategy of 2012; its workforce commitments carry no numbers, and the fiftieth-place ranking claimed for it is from a 2020 index edition ([strategy](2024-01-01-dgssi-strategie-nationale-cybersecurite-2030), [naming](2026-07-25-morocco-elected-african-telecommunications-union-council)).

The base had carried a 2023-dated account of a separate strategy; the full document confirms one instrument rather than two ([reconciliation](2024-01-01-dgssi-strategie-nationale-cybersecurite-2030)).

The national response centre issued a June 2026 advisory naming Moroccan institutions among about 75,000 devices affected in about 200 countries ([advisory](2026-06-21-hespress-morocco-fortibleed-macert-cyber-alert)); the base carries no dated record of the centre's creation ([advisory](2026-06-21-hespress-morocco-fortibleed-macert-cyber-alert)), and the security directive covering state bodies and vital infrastructures has been in force since January 2023 ([directive](2023-01-12-dgssi-circulaire-02-2023-directive-nationale-securite-si-v2)).

summary: A [national water digital twin](2026-07-28-morocco-water-digital-twin-national-data-platform-ehtp) is designed on a sovereign national data platform hosted domestically, with a first pilot put eighteen to twenty-four months away.
developments:
The three-layer design rests on a sovereign national data platform hosted in Morocco, fusing sensor networks, satellite observation and data from the basin agencies, the planning commission and engineering consultancies, and is to be hosted in an engineering school's forthcoming scientific tower ([design](2026-07-28-morocco-water-digital-twin-national-data-platform-ehtp)).

No cost, budget line or procurement route is given, and the platform it rests on is not otherwise recorded in this base, so the exchange layer appears here as a requirement of one project rather than as a standing national system.

summary: The police-run [trusted third-party verification platform](2025-05-05 Morocco boosts digital ID for government services (DGSN–Ministry partnership)) holds seventeen framework agreements with more than thirty authorised institutions, unchanged since 2024.
developments:
The platform reached its second phase with seventeen framework agreements and more than thirty authorised institutions, and a blueprint to extend verification to all government entities was recorded in May 2025 ([platform](2025-05-05 Morocco boosts digital ID for government services (DGSN–Ministry partnership)), [annual report](2024-12-24 Morocco's DGSN issued 4.6 million electronic national IDs in 2024 (annual report))).

No later agreement count, institution count or verification volume is held, so the reach of the country's identity verification into other systems is recorded as at 2024 and 2025.

summary: The [national health-data platform](2026-08-10-morocco-dhis2-health-data-audit) is in service and under a security and performance audit running from July to September 2026.
developments:
The audit covers infrastructure, application, database and cybersecurity, on a budget of 170,000 dirhams under a donor grant, with no cyberattack or breach cited as the trigger ([audit](2026-08-10-morocco-dhis2-health-data-audit)).

The budget and scope are the reporting outlet's account of the audit terms and no findings are published, so the base records that the platform exists and is being examined, and nothing about what it connects.

summary: The [identity and targeting project](2024-12-04 World Bank approves $70M for Morocco's social protection delivery (RNP and Unified Social Registry)) sets five social programmes using the registries by end-2024 and eight by 2028, with no delivery reported.
developments:
The project approved in December 2024 states those targets, with the two registries having enrolled about half the population at approval ([project](2024-12-04 World Bank approves $70M for Morocco's social protection delivery (RNP and Unified Social Registry)), [record](2024-01-01-world-bank-mar-2024-morocco-social-protection-identity-bw02)).

The end-2024 target date has passed and no count of programmes actually drawing on the registries is held, so the base records the design of the interoperability and no evidence of its use.

summary: The [national digital identity application](2025-09-24 Morocco fast-tracks 'Mon e-ID' digital identity after cyberattacks (iDAKTO)) reached 2.5m users and over 7m transactions by September 2025, accelerated after attacks on three state bodies.
developments:
Adoption was fast-tracked after cyberattacks on the social security fund, the justice ministry and the land registry ([acceleration](2025-09-24 Morocco fast-tracks 'Mon e-ID' digital identity after cyberattacks (iDAKTO))).

Usage stood at 2.5m users and more than 7m transactions since April 2022, and by February 2026 the same identity authenticates the national digital wallet ([partnership](2025-05-05 Morocco boosts digital ID for government services (DGSN–Ministry partnership))). It is vendor-built on an existing identity platform, and no availability, failure or fraud measure is published for it.

progress: No change, the newest issuance figure is for calendar 2024
summary: [4.6m electronic identity cards](2024-12-24 Morocco's DGSN issued 4.6 million electronic national IDs in 2024 (annual report)) were issued in 2024, including 219,408 for citizens abroad through seventy-one centres at diplomatic missions.
developments:
The police directorate's annual report gives 4.6m cards issued during 2024, with 219,408 issued to citizens abroad through 71 centres at diplomatic missions ([annual report](2024-12-24 Morocco's DGSN issued 4.6 million electronic national IDs in 2024 (annual report))).

No 2025 or 2026 issuance count is held ([institutional account](2024-09-18-maroc-digital-2030-plaquette-institutionnelle-en)), and no coverage share of the adult population is published, so the base holds a flow figure and not a stock one.

summary: A [biometric passport decree](2026-07-15-biometricupdate-morocco-biometric-passport-legal-framework) approved in July 2026 abolishes temporary passports and removes the address, and [identity-card renewal](2026-06-02-biometricupdate-morocco-national-id-renewal-online) moved online.
developments:
The decree specifies four languages including Amazigh, an encrypted chip, the address removed from the biodata page and temporary passports abolished, with the current format continuing during a transitional period; the joint body that sets issuance procedures is not yet in place ([decree](2026-07-15-biometricupdate-morocco-biometric-passport-legal-framework), [account](2026-07-10-en-hespress-morocco-new-biometric-passport-amazigh)).

Identity-card renewal moved online in mid-2026 with pre-fill, document upload, residency-certificate tracking and stamp-fee payment, biometric capture remaining in person; no take-up figure is held ([renewal](2026-06-02-biometricupdate-morocco-national-id-renewal-online), [announcement](2026-05-23-wearetech-morocco-digitizes-national-id-renewal)).

summary: Facial recognition is permitted case by case for [remote bank account opening](2020-04-23-cndp-deliberation-d-108-eus-2020-reconnaissance-faciale-compte-a-distance-banques) and [benefit proof of life](2020-07-29-cndp-deliberation-d-126-eus-2020-reconnaissance-faciale-preuve-de-vie-allocataires), both on prior authorisation since 2020.
developments:
Remote account opening was permitted by a deliberation of April 2020, conditional on a prior undertaking to migrate authentication to a future national trusted-third-party system that is not established as built ([banking](2020-04-23-cndp-deliberation-d-108-eus-2020-reconnaissance-faciale-compte-a-distance-banques)).

Proof of life for benefit recipients was permitted by a deliberation of July 2020 on the same migration condition, agreed with the insurance and social-security supervisor ([benefits](2020-07-29-cndp-deliberation-d-126-eus-2020-reconnaissance-faciale-preuve-de-vie-allocataires)). No authorisation count, revocation record or migration record is held for either.

summary: The [national digital wallet](2026-02-12-wearetech-morocco-idarati-x0-egov-architecture) binds five state bodies on a card-authenticated core, on eight partnership conventions signed in February 2026.
developments:
Eight conventions were signed in Rabat in February 2026 and two vendors engaged on architecture, on a stated six-month build ([conventions](2026-02-12-wearetech-morocco-idarati-x0-egov-architecture), [architecture](2026-02-12-biometricupdate-idakto-shareid-digital-wallet-superapp)).

The bodies bound are the social security fund, the road safety agency, the land registry, transport, and youth and culture. No launch date, service count or user figure is held, so the base records which systems have agreed to take the identity and not one that has.

summary: The central bank issued its [first standalone annual financial-inclusion report](2026-04-24-bkam-rapport-annuel-inclusion-financiere-exercice-2024) in April 2026, separate from the strategy implementation series it used to sit inside.
developments:
The report is explicitly separate from the national inclusion strategy's implementation series, which makes measurement a standing annual duty of the bank rather than a by-product of a programme ([report](2026-04-24-bkam-rapport-annuel-inclusion-financiere-exercice-2024)).

It names usage rather than access as what now limits inclusion, which is a judgement about the market and not only a count of it. No supervisory decision, licensing action or payment-system rule of the bank is separately held in this base.

summary: The registries served [5 million eligible households](2026-06-17 They're taking DPI to the world - The Times of India) on a June 2026 account, against about half the population enrolled at the end of 2024.
developments:
About half the population was enrolled when the second identity and targeting project was approved in December 2024 ([project](2024-12-04 World Bank approves $70M for Morocco's social protection delivery (RNP and Unified Social Registry))).

A June 2026 account puts 22 million of 39 million registered and 5 million eligible households served ([account](2026-06-17 They're taking DPI to the world - The Times of India)). It is a press figure rather than a programme report, and no payment volume or transfer value through the registries is held.

summary: A [merchant acquisition fund grant](2026-02-05-iati-46002-p-ma-h00-032-morocco-acquisition-fund-digital-payments) of about US$505,704 was committed for 2026 to 2028 through a continental digital financial inclusion facility.
developments:
The activity was reported at pipeline stage in February 2026, committing XDR 370,023.73, about US$505,704 at the provisional annual average rate, over 2026 to 2028 ([activity](2026-02-05-iati-46002-p-ma-h00-032-morocco-acquisition-fund-digital-payments)).

It responds to challenges the activity attributes to the central bank, and no disbursement transaction is reported. No merchant acceptance count or point-of-sale estate figure is held for the country.

summary: Wallets grew from [6.3m to 13.7m](2026-04-24-bkam-rapport-annuel-inclusion-financiere-exercice-2024) between 2021 and 2024 and account-holding from 53 to 58 per cent, on the central bank's own series.
developments:
Access points per 10,000 adults rose from about ten in 2021 to about fifteen in 2024, account-holding from 53 to 58 per cent, and wallets from 6.3m to 13.7m ([report](2026-04-24-bkam-rapport-annuel-inclusion-financiere-exercice-2024)); formal savings stood at 33 per cent and formal credit at 12 per cent of adults at the end of 2024 ([report](2026-04-24-bkam-rapport-annuel-inclusion-financiere-exercice-2024)).

The earlier strategy series runs wallets 2.44m in 2020, 6.3m in 2021, 7.7m in 2022 and 10.4m in 2023, with savings-account penetration reaching 38 per cent against a 20 per cent target ([strategy](2026-04-01-bkam-snif-rapport-annuel-exercice-2023)); microcredit stood at MAD 8.4bn in 2022 with active clients down 4.9 per cent to 795,000 ([strategy](2026-04-01-bkam-snif-rapport-annuel-exercice-2023), [earlier report](2021-01-01-bkam-snif-rapport-annuel-n3-2021)).

summary: [Law 72-18](2021-01-07-maroc-loi-72-18-ciblage-appui-social-agence-nationale-registres) creates the national population register and the agency to run it; the [agency](2024-12-04 World Bank approves $70M for Morocco's social protection delivery (RNP and Unified Social Registry)) has no establishment date, budget or operating record.
developments:
The statute creates the population register, the unified social register and a national register agency, with article 45 deferring force to implementing texts ([statute](2021-01-07-maroc-loi-72-18-ciblage-appui-social-agence-nationale-registres)).

The agency was named in December 2024 as a component of the identity and targeting project to be operationalised, and nothing since records it established ([agency](2024-12-04 World Bank approves $70M for Morocco's social protection delivery (RNP and Unified Social Registry))). So the register operates and the body the law puts in charge of it does not yet exist.

summary: The population and unified social registries hold [22 million of 39 million](2026-06-17 They're taking DPI to the world - The Times of India) on a June 2026 account, built on an open-source identity platform adopted in 2018.
developments:
Enrolment stood at about half the population when the second identity and targeting project was approved in December 2024 ([approval](2024-12-04 World Bank approves $70M for Morocco's social protection delivery (RNP and Unified Social Registry))).

A June 2026 account gives 22 million of 39 million registered, on a platform the country adopted first, in 2018 ([account](2026-06-17 They're taking DPI to the world - The Times of India)). The figure reaches the base through the press rather than a programme report, and no error, exclusion or appeal measure for the registries is held.

summary: [Online registration](2026-01-14 Morocco — 16.5m voters on electoral rolls; most 2026 registrations via digital channels) took two of every three new entries in the 2026 revision, and an [organic law](2025-11-29-morocco-rapport-commission-lecture1-loi-55-25-chambre-des-representants) institutionalises internet-based enrolment.
developments:
The interior minister's account of the annual revision records new registrations running two to one in favour of the online channel over in-person enrolment, on a roll of about 16.5m voters with about 1.4m entries removed ([revision](2026-01-14 Morocco — 16.5m voters on electoral rolls; most 2026 registrations via digital channels)).

Organic law 55.25 institutionalises internet-based electoral-roll registration for residents and expatriates and bars artificial-intelligence tools and social platforms from publishing referendum poll results; it was adopted in committee across four sessions in November 2025 and companion law 54.25 was constitutionally cleared in December ([committee report](2025-11-29-morocco-rapport-commission-lecture1-loi-55-25-chambre-des-representants), [decision](2025-12-24-maroc-cour-constitutionnelle-decision-260-25-loi-organique-54-25)).

summary: The interior ministry began a [nationwide screening of collective land community rolls](2026-08-22-morocco-interior-screens-collective-land-community-rolls) in August 2026, on a single methodology for the first time.
developments:
Circulars went to community delegates through local authority officials from 22 August 2026, beginning in two regions and open to extension nationwide ([screening](2026-08-22-morocco-interior-screens-collective-land-community-rolls)).

Each listed member is to be verified for actual affiliation, legal majority and residence under law 62.17 and its implementing decree, applying one methodology so that criteria stop varying from one community to another. No count of communities, members or corrections is published.

summary: A [digital health bill](2026-07-23-morocco-draft-law-52-26-digital-health-shared-record-unique-id) creating a [shared medical record](2026-08-06-numeriser-le-parcours-sante-oui-terroriser-les-medecins-non) has been adopted and is publicly opposed by doctors over its penal chapter.
developments:
The fifty-article bill sets implementing decrees due within twelve months of publication and provider connection within twenty-four months of the technical decree, and its text is not published ([bill](2026-07-23-morocco-draft-law-52-26-digital-health-shared-record-unique-id)).

Its penal chapter runs from six to twelve months and MAD 50,000 to 200,000 under one article to MAD 50,000 to 300,000 for failure to feed or interconnect the record under another ([penal chapter](2026-07-23-morocco-draft-law-52-26-digital-health-shared-record-unique-id)).

A doctors' and clinics' collective opposes it, citing leaks at the social security fund, and doctors protested in August 2026 ([opposition](2026-08-06-numeriser-le-parcours-sante-oui-terroriser-les-medecins-non), [protest](2026-08-17-hespress-doctors-protest-health-digitization-bill-5226)). With the text unpublished, neither the objection nor the answer to it can be checked against what the law says.

summary: The tax directorate began [matching declared income against records held by other administrations](2026-08-20-morocco-tax-authority-matches-income-property-data) in August 2026, opening audit files on an initial 87 taxpayers.
developments:
Regional and national control services compared declarations of total income against records of activities, property, transactions and investments registered in taxpayers' names and held by other administrations and institutions ([matching](2026-08-20-morocco-tax-authority-matches-income-property-data)).

Audit files were opened on an initial 87 liberal-profession taxpayers, and the checks extend beyond professional income to agricultural and real-estate earnings, with corrections to the tax base expected. The administrations supplying the matched data are not named, so the exchange is visible in its effect and not in its plumbing.

summary: The only record of the [single-window trade platform](2016-10-27 New plan and updated legislation provide a boost for Morocco's IT sector (Oxford Business Group)) is a 2016 reference survey putting 18,000 importers and exporters on it.
developments:
The platform carried 18,000 importers and exporters in 2016 and no figure or status has been published since ([survey](2016-10-27 New plan and updated legislation provide a boost for Morocco's IT sector (Oxford Business Group))).

Ten years is a long time for a customs platform to go unmeasured in a base otherwise rich in regulator and ministry series, so the gap here is one of collection rather than of activity.

progress: Regressed, on the availability of a service the state runs
summary: [600 services are online](2026-02-12-wearetech-morocco-idarati-x0-egov-architecture), [22 certificates were abolished](2026-07-25-morocco-abolishes-22-certificates-law-55-19-idarati) under the simplification law, and the [procedures portal](2026-07-25-morocco-abolishes-22-certificates-law-55-19-idarati) carries over 2,500 transcribed procedures.
developments:
The official e-visa portal failed from 20 August 2026, freezing after the travel-conditions step so applicants could not reach the personal-details stage ([report](2026-08-27-visasupdate-morocco-e-visa-portal-disruption)). No restoration date and no official acknowledgement is in the base.

Law 55.19 has been in force since September 2020 and created the procedures portal by its article 26: only procedures published there are legally recognised and enforceable on citizen and official alike, certified copies and legalised signatures are dropped for most procedures, and no administration may demand more than one copy of a file ([law](2026-07-25-morocco-abolishes-22-certificates-law-55-19-idarati)).

The ministry reports a 45 per cent reduction in documents demanded of users where its simplification method has been applied, on perimeters it does not name ([method](2024-05-01-mtnra-guide-methodologique-simplification-digitalisation-parcours-usagers)). An interior ministry circular abolished 22 certificates in 2026 and replaced them with sworn declarations ([circular](2026-07-25-morocco-abolishes-22-certificates-law-55-19-idarati)).

The medical council put registration, transfers, licence changes and fee payment online in August 2026, implementing a mandate set by decree in 2016 ([platform](2026-08-06-morocco-cnom-digital-platform)), and 600 services were counted online in February 2026 ([count](2026-02-12-wearetech-morocco-idarati-x0-egov-architecture)).

progress: No change, both figures are from 2024 and the stated extension target has passed
summary: [80 mobile identity enrolment units](2024-12-24 Morocco's DGSN issued 4.6 million electronic national IDs in 2024 (annual report)) served more than 130,000 citizens in 2024, and [registry extension to remote areas](2024-12-04 World Bank approves $70M for Morocco's social protection delivery (RNP and Unified Social Registry)) has no delivery figure.
developments:
The mobile units are the base's only Morocco-specific rural digital-delivery instrument: 80 units serving more than 130,000 citizens in 2024, with no later figure held ([units](2024-12-24 Morocco's DGSN issued 4.6 million electronic national IDs in 2024 (annual report))).

Extension of the registries to rural and remote areas via digital and remote applications was a component of the December 2024 project, with at least five programmes targeted by end-2024 and eight by 2028; that target date has passed with no delivery or coverage figure held ([extension](2024-12-04 World Bank approves $70M for Morocco's social protection delivery (RNP and Unified Social Registry))).

summary: The country [rose fourteen places to 87th](2026-08-10-morocco-ai-data-center-investment-northafricapost) on a government artificial-intelligence readiness index, and signed a [cooperation agreement](2026-05-07-techreviewafrica-morocco-african-open-government-conference) on artificial-intelligence tools for corruption-risk prevention.
developments:
The 2025 index edition puts the country 87th globally and eighth in its region, up fourteen places, attributed in the account to the national roadmap and a regional data-for-sustainable-development hub developed with UNDP; the index is not named in the record held and the starting position is derived from the reported change ([index](2026-08-10-morocco-ai-data-center-investment-northafricapost)).

A cooperation agreement with the anti-corruption authority was signed in May 2026, aiming at transparency through advanced information systems and artificial-intelligence tools for corruption-risk prevention ([agreement](2026-05-07-techreviewafrica-morocco-african-open-government-conference)). No deployed administrative system using the technology is separately recorded.

summary: [Four artificial-intelligence institutes](2026-08-15-morocco-jazari-ai-institutes-established) were established by gazette in August 2026, after a [founding institute and four regional or thematic agreements](2026-01-12-mtnra-ai-made-in-morocco-jazari-root-launch).
developments:
Four public-interest institutes were established by publication in the official gazette, covering research and sovereign systems, education, industrial automation and smart cities, with no budget, staffing or opening date stated ([establishment](2026-08-15-morocco-jazari-ai-institutes-established)).

A founding institute launched in January 2026, and four regional or thematic institutes had been constituted by protocol or founding agreement between April 2025 and March 2026 ([founding](2026-01-12-mtnra-ai-made-in-morocco-jazari-root-launch), [industry institute](2026-03-11-techafricanews-ai-made-in-morocco-industry-x0)).

The regional protocols were signed nine months before the founding institute, and no statute, legal form, campus, governance structure or intake was published for any of them until the gazette ([Dakhla](2025-11-18-techreviewafrica-morocco-green-data-center-ai-institute-dakhla)).

summary: A [national responsible-artificial-intelligence platform](2025-09-11-en-hespress-morocco-responsible-ai-platform-deal) was agreed between the ministry and the data-protection commission in September 2025, with nothing built eleven months later.
developments:
The agreement commits the two bodies to build national platforms on large language models incorporating Moroccan language, culture, legal framework and digital identity ([agreement](2025-09-11-en-hespress-morocco-responsible-ai-platform-deal)).

No platform, budget or delivery date is on record eleven months after signature, so the country's principal instrument for governing the technology in use is an undertaking between two institutions rather than a working control.

progress: Mixed, a large offshoring base whose last published outturn is for 2024, against new agreements targeting 2030
summary: Digital offshoring stood at [148,500 employed and MAD 26.2bn of exports](2026-01-30-wearetech-morocco-three-deals-digital-offshoring) at end-2024, with [three agreements](2026-01-30-wearetech-morocco-three-deals-digital-offshoring) targeting 270,000 jobs by 2030.
developments:
The end-2024 outturn is 148,500 employed and MAD 26.2bn of exports, and no newer figure has been published ([outturn](2026-01-30-wearetech-morocco-three-deals-digital-offshoring)); no official statistical release on the sector is held at all ([outturn](2026-01-30-wearetech-morocco-three-deals-digital-offshoring)).

Three agreements signed in Rabat in January 2026 cover a training incentive, territorial attractiveness and specialised offshoring hubs, on a stated 2030 target of 270,000 jobs and nearly MAD 40bn in exports ([agreements](2026-01-30-wearetech-morocco-three-deals-digital-offshoring)); the texts are not held ([agreements](2026-01-30-wearetech-morocco-three-deals-digital-offshoring)).

A vendor inaugurated a regional research and development office at Agadir in June 2026, with no headcount or investment figure published for it, and a Casablanca centre announced in 2025 with 1,000 jobs claimed has no outturn on file ([office](2026-06-30-techreviewafrica-oracle-rd-office-agadir), [announcement](2025-06-26-wearetech-morocco-attracts-major-tech-players)).

summary: A [fintech centre](2025-06-10-techreviewafrica-morocco-fintech-ecosystem-ai-inclusion) operates with no published figures, and an [artificial-intelligence start-up programme](2026-04-09-techafricanews-orange-maroc-technopark-ai) with a technology park was announced in April 2026.
developments:
The fintech centre was named by the minister at a payments industry event in June 2025, with no participant, funding or output figure held then or since; a start-up support programme is named alongside it, also without figures ([centre](2025-06-10-techreviewafrica-morocco-fintech-ecosystem-ai-inclusion)).

The start-up programme announced at an April 2026 exhibition offers cloud, connectivity, cybersecurity and business use cases to artificial-intelligence start-ups, with no cohort, intake or budget published and nothing on file since ([programme](2026-04-09-techafricanews-orange-maroc-technopark-ai)).

progress: No change, the start-up count has not been republished since January 2025
summary: The development agency's database lists [1,028 start-ups](2025-01-03-add-base-de-donnees-startups-marocaines) on a January 2025 release, and a [govtech challenge](2026-07-22-morocco-govtech-innovation-challenge-2026-seco-world-bank) opened a public sourcing channel in July 2026.
developments:
The 2024 file released on the national open-data portal carries 1,028 entries, the union of four listing exercises, with no funding amounts, no definition of a start-up and unnormalised city and sector fields, so the number is a count of rows ([database](2025-01-03-add-base-de-donnees-startups-marocaines)).

A GovTech Innovation Challenge was launched in Rabat in July 2026 as a sourcing channel for public-audit and public financial management tools, with the general finance inspectorate and the court of audit as institutional users and no budget or timetable announced ([challenge](2026-07-22-morocco-govtech-innovation-challenge-2026-seco-world-bank)).

summary: An [executive cybersecurity programme](2026-06-02-assabah-rabat-cybersecurity-leadership-program) for African officials ran in Rabat in June 2026, and a [skills memorandum](2026-07-20-maroc-capgemini-ia-memorandum) covers acculturation across administrations.
developments:
The five-day programme for senior officials of African member states was organised by the continental network of cybersecurity authorities and hosted by the national information systems security directorate, with no participant count or budget stated ([programme](2026-06-02-assabah-rabat-cybersecurity-leadership-program)).

A memorandum signed in Rabat in July 2026 covers skills-building and acculturation across administrations, universities and research centres, support to institute-backed start-ups, and public-service use cases, with no sum attached ([memorandum](2026-07-20-maroc-capgemini-ia-memorandum)). Neither carries a count of officials trained.

summary: The [national literacy strategy to 2035](2023-01-01-anlca-strategie-nationale-alphabetisation-2023-2035) names a digital element among its strategic choices, and citizen-level digital literacy remains an absence in this base.
developments:
The strategy runs from 2023 to 2035 and is delivered through a roadmap covering 2023 to 2027 ([strategy](2023-01-01-anlca-strategie-nationale-alphabetisation-2023-2035)).

Its eighth strategic choice names a digital element that is not established in the French text held, and no programme, participant count or digital-skills measurement for the general population is held elsewhere in the base.

progress: Advanced, on a figure that has not been republished since the 2023-24 academic year
summary: Enrolment in public-university digital streams [doubled to 21,125](2024-09-24-mtnra-brochure-digital-talents) in 2023-24, alongside 183 newly accredited digital degree programmes.
developments:
The ministry's digital talent brochure gives 21,125 enrolled in 2023-24, up from 10,712 the year before, with 183 newly accredited digital degree programmes and 1,000 people trained through a placement programme by the end of August 2024 ([brochure](2024-09-24-mtnra-brochure-digital-talents)).

The figures are ministry-reported and no later enrolment count has been published, so the base holds one year-on-year doubling and nothing after it.

summary: A [national research and innovation programme](2025-04-08-maroc-ma-lancement-officiel-pnardi-2025-2028) commits MAD 1bn across four editions to 2028, with no digital or artificial-intelligence share stated.
developments:
The programme has been in force since April 2025, funded jointly by the higher-education ministry and an industrial group, with MAD 1bn across four editions between 2025 and 2028 of which MAD 200m is directed at mobilising Moroccan researchers resident abroad ([launch](2025-04-08-maroc-ma-lancement-officiel-pnardi-2025-2028)).

The first edition's three sub-programmes, covering research and development, young researchers and technology transfer, opened for applications between June and October 2025 ([call](2025-06-03-cnrst-masharie-pnardi-2025-2028-programme)). No award or disbursement record is held, and no digital share of the fund is stated.

progress: Mixed, a police reporting platform in service against an ombudsman caseload up more than a quarter
summary: The ombudsman opened [9,958 files in 2025](2026-07-23-morocco-ombudsman-2025-report-bureaucracy-citizen-services), up more than a quarter, while a [police reporting platform](2024-12-24 Morocco's DGSN issued 4.6 million electronic national IDs in 2024 (annual report)) has taken 12,614 reports since June 2024.
developments:
The ombudsman's 2025 report gives 9,958 files opened, 1,653 settlement decisions, a mean 815 days to implement a recommendation and 774 days to close a file ending in one ([report](2026-07-23-morocco-ombudsman-2025-report-bureaucracy-citizen-services)); the base holds press accounts of the report rather than the report ([report](2026-07-23-morocco-ombudsman-2025-report-bureaucracy-citizen-services), [account](2026-07-24-morocco-azendour-ombudsman-report-administrative-failures)).

The police reporting platform launched in June 2024 and had taken 12,614 reports by the end of that year, with no later count held ([platform](2024-12-24 Morocco's DGSN issued 4.6 million electronic national IDs in 2024 (annual report))).

summary: An [online proxy-voting platform](2026-08-23-morocco-interior-voter-notification-proxy-voting-platform) for citizens resident abroad opened in August 2026 for the September legislative elections.
developments:
The platform runs from 24 August 2026 until noon on 22 September under organic law 27.11: the voter abroad names a proxy registered on a domestic electoral roll, certifies the mandate personally, then downloads and sends the mandate on to the proxy ([platform](2026-08-23-morocco-interior-voter-notification-proxy-voting-platform)).

Polling-station notifications are delivered over the same period, and the ministry stressed that the notification is not required to vote, the national identity card remaining the only accepted proof of identity at the polling station.

summary: An [insurance technology and inclusion programme](2026-04-23-iati-46002-p-ma-h00-029-morocco-insurtech-ecosystem-innovation) targets about 200,000 new insurance users of whom at least 100,000 are to be women.
developments:
The activity was reported at pipeline stage in April 2026, committing XDR 371,714.70, about US$508,015 at the provisional annual average rate, over 2026 to 2028 and executed by the insurance supervisor ([activity](2026-04-23-iati-46002-p-ma-h00-029-morocco-insurtech-ecosystem-innovation)); total cost is US$680,000, of which US$510,000 is grant and US$170,000 counterpart ([activity](2026-04-23-iati-46002-p-ma-h00-029-morocco-insurtech-ecosystem-innovation)).

It is the only gender target in the base's digital record for the country, and it is a target rather than an outturn: no sex-disaggregated measure of access, use or ownership is held.

progress: No change, a first company-reported figure with no earlier year behind it
summary: The only device-cost measure on file is an operator [refurbishing 6,000 internet boxes](2026-07-17-orange-reconditionne-164000-box-internet) in 2025, saving a reported EUR 1.5m.
developments:
An operator sustainability report published in July 2026 gives 6,000 boxes refurbished in Morocco during 2025 with EUR 1.5m in savings, company-reported ([report](2026-07-17-orange-reconditionne-164000-box-internet)).

Only the group figure of 164,000 boxes across Africa and the Middle East carries a prior year ([group figure](2026-07-17-orange-reconditionne-164000-box-internet)), so the Moroccan number has no direction. No urban-rural, income or gender divide measure is held for the country.

summary: The [national open-data portal](2026-08-08-data-gov-ma-gouvernance-plan-actions-national-open-data) operates with a documented publication procedure, and its published datasets include a [1,028-entry start-up database](2025-01-03-add-base-de-donnees-startups-marocaines).
developments:
The portal has run with a documented publication procedure since April 2021 and its governance was documented in August 2026, with a steering committee of ten bodies coordinated by the development agency ([governance](2026-08-08-data-gov-ma-gouvernance-plan-actions-national-open-data), [manual](2021-04-01-add-maroc-ouverture-donnees-publiques-manuel-responsables-open-data)).

Its published datasets include a start-up database of 1,028 entries released in January 2025 ([dataset](2025-01-03-add-base-de-donnees-startups-marocaines)).

The portal's own dataset count, publication statistics and open-data action plan are not held, so the base can describe how publication is governed and not how much is published.

summary: Two national [earth-observation satellites](2024-06-01-morocco-copuos-67-statement-space-sustainable-development) launched in 2017 and 2018 support applications named in water, land use, agriculture and disaster management.
developments:
The country's own statement to the United Nations committee on the peaceful uses of outer space names the two satellites, operated by the royal remote sensing centre, and the application areas they serve ([statement](2024-06-01-morocco-copuos-67-statement-space-sustainable-development)).

No product, user, coverage or accuracy figure is published for the agricultural use, so the base records a capability and not its application to a crop, a season or a decision.

progress: Mixed, a research office opened while two announced cloud regions have no launch record
summary: A vendor [opened a regional research office](2026-06-30-techreviewafrica-oracle-rd-office-agadir) in June 2026, while its [two announced cloud regions](2025-07-31 Morocco Digital Economy — US Country Commercial Guide (Digital Morocco 2030)) have no record of entering service, under a [science and technology framework](2023-07-28-tias-23-728-us-morocco-science-technology-cooperation-protocol).
developments:
Two cloud regions were announced in May 2024 at about US$140m over five years, and no held source records either entering service ([regions](2025-07-31 Morocco Digital Economy — US Country Commercial Guide (Digital Morocco 2030))); what the base establishes is the absence of a launch record, not that the regions failed to open ([regions](2025-07-31 Morocco Digital Economy — US Country Commercial Guide (Digital Morocco 2030))).

The same vendor's regional research and development office was inaugurated at Agadir by the head of government in June 2026 ([office](2026-06-30-techreviewafrica-oracle-rd-office-agadir)).

A bilateral science and technology agreement is in force under a 2023 protocol; its signed pages carry no text layer, so its operative terms and term of years are not established, and it is a science framework rather than a digital instrument ([protocol](2023-07-28-tias-23-728-us-morocco-science-technology-cooperation-protocol)).

summary: The only Chinese engagement on file is a vendor [dual-band radio deployment](2026-07-30-inwi-partners-with-huawei-to-boost-mobile-coverage-across-moroccos-rail-and-highway-networks) on rail and motorway corridors, in commercial service in 2026.
developments:
An operator and a Chinese vendor put the first commercial deployment of a 1.8 GHz and 2.1 GHz configuration into service on rail and motorway corridors, claiming a 13 dB coverage gain, 83 per cent higher average downlink throughput and 3.2 times the active users with no additional sites built ([deployment](2026-08-13-morocco-inwi-huawei-transport-route-coverage), [partnership](2026-07-30-inwi-partners-with-huawei-to-boost-mobile-coverage-across-moroccos-rail-and-highway-networks)).

Every performance figure is the operator's and the vendor's own and is unverified. No Chinese state instrument, loan or technology cooperation framework for the country is held.

summary: EUR20m of the 2026 EU action programme was reserved to the digital partnership ([programme](2026-08-26-morocco-eu-pap-num-5g-financing)).
developments:
The European Commission reserved EUR20m of a maximum EUR148m 2026 action programme to the digital partnership support programme ([programme](2026-08-26-morocco-eu-pap-num-5g-financing)).

The Commission's list of recognised third countries, current to August 2026, names sixteen jurisdictions plus one international organisation, none of them in Africa; an intention to seek adequacy was reported during 2025 ([list](2026-08-05-european-commission-adequacy-decisions-list), [roundup](2026-01-11 The Year of the Teeth Data Protection in Africa Roundup, 2025, Projections for 2026)).

Convention 108 was ratified during 2019, the exact date not held ([accession](2012-10-18-coe-tpd-2012-09rev-avis-adhesion-maroc-convention-108)). Neither adequacy source is tagged to the country, and no Morocco-tagged governance source in the base mentions the European Union at all, which is itself the finding.

summary: The country is [turning to India](2026-08-26-maroc-inde-ia-langues-nationales) to develop artificial intelligence adapted to its national languages, on an August 2026 report.
developments:
The turn to India was reported in August 2026 as a stated direction rather than an agreement ([report](2026-08-26-maroc-inde-ia-langues-nationales)).

No instrument, partner institution, language list, budget or timetable is published, so the base records an intention and nothing that would let a later run check whether it was acted on.
